lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN
lead.headline: Missiles Hit an Oil Building in Saudi Arabia
lead.deck: Saudi Arabia says a Houthi missile struck an Aramco office in Dhahran on Tuesday.
body: Saudi Arabia is fighting a war with the Houthis, a group in Yemen. Yemen is the country just south of Saudi Arabia. On Saturday, a missile hit the main airport in Riyadh, the Saudi capital. Saudi officials say at least 13 people were killed and more than 300 were hurt.

The fighting has now reached an oil company. On Tuesday, a missile hit an office building at Aramco’s base in Dhahran. Aramco is Saudi Arabia’s giant oil company. Saudi news said there was a small fire and nobody was hurt. The Houthis say they did it, and they promise more attacks on Saudi airports and oil sites.

Saudi Arabia is hitting back. It struck an oil site near Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, on Tuesday. President Trump says the United States is thinking about joining the Saudi side. When he was asked, he said, “We may.” The US Embassy in Riyadh has told Americans to reconsider travelling to Saudi Arabia. Riyadh’s airport is closed until at least Saturday.

lead.why: Oil and airports are things many countries rely on. When they are hit, people far from Yemen can feel it.

world.headline: Hurricane Isaias Leaves Six Dead in Florida
world.deck: Tens of thousands of homes are still without power after the storm.
body: Hurricane Isaias, a huge spinning storm, hit Florida near the city of Destin on Friday night. It was a Category 2 storm, with gusts of up to 118 miles an hour.

The danger did not end with the wind. On Tuesday, Governor Ron DeSantis said six people had died in Florida. Two more died in Alabama. Some deaths came from falling trees. Others came when people could not get medical care.
Power is the next problem. At the worst point, more than 400,000 customers lost electricity. By Tuesday, about 95 percent had it back, but over 45,000 were still waiting.

fact_or_fiction.claim: The US Embassy in Riyadh has told Americans to reconsider travelling to Saudi Arabia. Riyadh’s airport is closed until at least Saturday.
fact_or_fiction.why: Saudi aviation extended the shutdown through 17 October.

fact_or_fiction.claim: Hurricane Isaias hit Florida near the city of Miami.
fact_or_fiction.why: It came ashore near Destin, on Florida’s Gulf Coast.

fact_or_fiction.claim: By Tuesday, about 95 percent of Florida customers who lost power had it back.
fact_or_fiction.why: Over 45,000 were still waiting, mostly on the Panhandle.
